'''Takeoshi Yama Tarine''' (建忍山垂根) is a figure mentioned in ancient Japanese texts such as the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}''. He is regarded as the progenitor of the {{ill|Hozumi clan|ja|穂積氏}}.

== Genealogy ==
The genealogy of Takeoshi Yama Tarine is not detailed in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' or the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}''. However, he is identified as the father of {{ill|Oto-takara|ja|弟財郎女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otodokoro no Iratsume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q20039293}}, who became an empress of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|en|Emperor Seimu|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}.

He is also recognized as the father of the sisters {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|大橘比売命|lt=Otachibana-hime no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|弟橘媛|lt=Princess Ototachibana}}, both of whom are associated with the legendary prince {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|倭建命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} as recorded in the ''Kojiki'', ''Nihon Shoki'', and ''{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|常陸国風土記}}''.

== Historical Mentions ==
In the ''Kojiki'' section about Emperor Seimu, Takeoshi Yama Tarine is introduced as the father of {{ill|Oto-takara|ja|弟財郎女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otodokoro no Iratsume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q20039293}}, a consort of the emperor. Additionally, he is described in the ''Kojiki'', ''Nihon Shoki'', and ''Hitachi Fudoki'' as the father of {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|大橘比売命|lt=Otachibana-hime no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Tachibanahime-no-Mikoto|ja|弟橘媛|lt=Princess Ototachibana}}. These sisters are featured prominently in the mythology surrounding Yamato Takeru.

Takeoshi Yama Tarine is enshrined as a deity at {{ill|Hozumi Shrine|ja|穂積神社}} and {{ill|Oshiyama Shrine|ja|忍山神社}}.
